correctness.rationale: The seven-point binary-dot-product incidence representation defines exactly 21 Heawood graph edges and a genuine order-two polarity. Geometric fixed barycentric coordinates identify its fixed realization with the simplicial complex of allowable edge orbits. The independent original matching and orbit-model enumerators match on all 138 invariant faces. The twelve-orbit complex has 137 nonempty faces, 351 Hasse covers, and an explicitly listed 66-pair acyclic matching, verified by a full directed topological sort, leaving a single vertex and four two-simplices. The discrete Morse CW complex is therefore exactly a wedge of four two-spheres over the integers. Independent mod-two ranks 11, 34, 21 corroborate but are not substituted for the integral homotopy proof.

originality.rationale: No checked record states or implies the canonical Heawood polarity geometric fixed-space integral homotopy. The public ordinary-complex classification gives sixteen four-spheres; its full rational automorphism character gives only trace four for colour-reversing involutions and hence fixed-space Euler characteristic five. Neither determines degree-two homotopy, fundamental group or torsion of the geometric fixed space. The separately classified perfect-matching subcomplex has different allowed faces and does not imply the result. The recent motivating primary paper studies distinct Möbius/circular ladder graphs. Direct equivalence, broader theorem, and exact-table queries found no covering published claim; unindexed equivalents remain a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper, book or differently expressed automorphism-fixed matching complex result may already contain an equivalent homotopy calculation.
The present finite computer-assisted acyclicity certificate has not been independently audited by another mathematician.
No general claim about other polarities, automorphism conjugacy classes, or higher-order projective planes is supported.

value.rationale: The canonical orthogonal polarity is a distinguished point-line duality of the smallest projective plane, and the Heawood graph is its natural incidence graph. The fixed geometric matching complex is a intrinsic symmetry invariant of this highly symmetric graph. A previously determined trace four gives only Euler characteristic five; the new integral sphere-wedge identifies simple connectivity, degree-two generators, zero other homology, and no torsion. The small twelve-orbit model and complete 66-pair Morse certificate make the invariant directly reproducible. This is motivated by symmetry topology and the gap between character and fixed-space homotopy, not a routine incremental size case.
